items.title: Anthropic 介绍 Claude Duet 智能体的安全、隐私与凭证隔离设计
items.description: Anthropic 发文介绍处于研究预览阶段的 Claude Duet 智能体的安全与隐私设计。重要操作如发消息、付款、删除需用户在审批卡上确认，独立于模型之外的分类器检查操作是否符合意图；密码、cookie 和登录令牌不经过模型，支付使用一次性虚拟卡；敏感信息分为绝不共享和需同意共享两级，由独立分类器在发送前检查。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g9tc56izmwy49zgw5ta4ubsya

items.title: 消息称字节跳动 AI 短剧产品内部整合：小云雀并入即梦，仍保留独立入口
items.description: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，据 36 氪今日报道，字节跳动内部近期完成了一次业务整合，AI 短剧创作平台小云雀并入智能创作平台即梦，产品仍保留独立入口。 此次调整以资源整合为主，即梦已经接入小云雀的短剧相关能力。调整后，小云雀的运营由即梦运营和市场负责人陈欣然负责，产品团队没有变化。 小云雀和即梦均出自字节剪映团队。小云雀定位为一站式 AI 内容创作平台，今年 3 月上线短剧 Agent，支持上传最多 10 万字剧本、一键生成视频成片，搭载了字节自研的 Seedance 2.0 模型，在短剧、漫剧的标准化生产场景中具备从剧本解析到分镜生成的完整流程能力。 即梦 AI 于 2024 年 5 月推出，最初覆盖文生图、文生视频等生成能力，此后逐步向智能画布、首尾帧控制等偏专业创作的 Agent 编辑工具延伸，用户群体覆盖普通创作者与专业设计师。 IT之家注意到，两者在功能上存在重叠：都能在平台内完成“从生成到成片”的全流程，与剪映的剪辑环节形成平行的用户路径。

items.title: 腾讯 WorkBuddy 接入模型 Kimi-K3.1-Pro，支持 100 万上下文

items.title: 瑞典政府办公厅出手，禁止办公电脑直接访问 ChatGPT、Claude
items.description: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，当地时间 23 日，据瑞典国家公共广播公司 Sveriges Radio 报道，瑞典政府办公厅将从下周一起禁止工作人员 通过办公电脑直接访问 ChatGPT 和 Claude ，要求员工改用微软 Copilot 等获得批准的 AI 服务。 内部资料显示，该国政府办公厅还对 Copilot 进行了审查，并进一步加强了安全防护。该机构数字化总监米卡埃尔 · 韦特克兰茨（Mikael Wettercrantz）在政府办公厅内网上指出，使用未签订协议的 AI 服务可能 对信息安全造成影响 。 调查发现，瑞典税务局和国家机构管理局（SiS）也已采取类似的封锁措施。瑞典强制执行局则尚未作出决定，仍在研究是否实施限制。 瑞典多家政府机构都注意到了 未经规范管理的 AI 使用行为所带来的风险 ，并采取了其他应对措施。瑞典交通管理局就是其中之一。今年早些时候，该机构内部审计发现，员工普遍使用约 10 种 AI 服务，其中存在不少风险。 审计报告指出：“我们发现了多个使用开放式 AI 服务时出现问题的案例。问题既涉及输入信息的敏感程度，也涉及 AI 生成回答的处理方式。”

On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post . AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv , a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”

Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision.
